Commentary.Commentary: It has been a day of the debutants for the New Zealand side so far. Ferguson and Wheeler were right on the money and took three and two wickets apiece. Santner and Grandhomme bowled tight spells as well. The Kiwis are firm favourites going into the break. Is there a twist in the tale awaiting? Let's see if the tourists can come out and throw surprises. Join us for the second innings in a short while.

A good flourish from Mahmudullah in the end has led Bangladesh to a modest total of 141 on the board. He had a poor outing with the bat in the ODI series and has begun the new year with a sensible fifty. He was the only one who played with sanity and ensured that the scoreboard kept ticking. Still, the target of 142 is below par on a track where the ball is coming nicely onto the bat and with brutal hitters in the opposition ranks this could prove to be tough to defend.
OUT b Lockie Ferguson. Bangladesh have lost their eighth wicket.
OUT c Colin de Grandhomme b Ben Wheeler. Bangladesh have lost their seventh wicket.
OUT c Corey Anderson b Mitchell Santner. Bangladesh have lost their sixth wicket.

UPDATE 11-15 overs, BAN 97/5 - Shakib's lean patch with the bat continues and he has gifted his wicket away. The Bangladeshi batsmen never kept going and the failure to construct a substantial partnership has put a lid on their run flow. Grandhomme and Santner have kept it tight and made life difficult for the tourists. The only positives for the visitors is that Mahmudullah is still out there and Mosaddek has hit a couple of lusty blows. Can they score briskly in the last 5 overs and change the momentum or will the hosts run away with the show? Due to the lack of television feed there won't be any commentary for this game but we will provide you with updates every 5 overs.
OUT c Mitchell Santner b Colin de Grandhomme. Bangladesh have lost their fifth wicket.

UPDATE 6-10 overs, BAN 65/4 - It is turning to be a dream start for Ferguson. He has picked up two wickets in the first two balls of his T20I debut and has dented the middle order. Bangladesh have pushed themselves further into a hole. It was a really soft dismissal for Rahman while Sarkar was welcomed with a peach and he went back for a duck. A bit of steadiness is returning with Mahmudullah and Shakib in the middle. Will they be able  to turn it around in the next phase? Due to the lack of television feed there won't be any commentary for this game but we will provide you with updates every 5 overs.
OUT c Corey Anderson b Lockie Ferguson. Bangladesh have lost their fourth wicket.
OUT c Matt Henry b Lockie Ferguson. Bangladesh have lost their third wicket.

UPDATE 1-5 overs, BAN - 30/2 - Just the start the Kiwis would have wanted. The debutant, Ben Wheeler and Matt Henry have hit the deck hard and have got the ball to swing appreciably. The moisture on the pitch due to the earlier rains have helped their cause and they have given away very little. Both have been rewarded with a wicket for their disciplined lines and lengths. On the other hand, the Bangladeshi batsmen have been too rash from the word go. Imrul Kayes went for a wild slog across the line and threw away his wicket in the second over itself and Tamim Iqbal followed him with a poor shot. Shakib Al Hasan has joined Sabbir Rahman in the middle and they need to stitch together a crucial partnership to claw back into the contest. Let's see how the game unfolds. Due to the lack of television feed there won't be any commentary for this game but we will provide you with updates every 5 overs.
OUT c Tom Bruce b Ben Wheeler. Bangladesh have lost their second wicket.
OUT c Luke Ronchi b Matt Henry. Bangladesh have lost their first wicket.
New Zealand Playing XI - Kane Williamson(c), Neil Broom, Colin Munro, Corey Anderson, Tom Bruce, Colin de Grandhomme, Luke Ronchi(w), Mitchell Santner, Ben Wheeler, Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson.

Bangladesh Playing XI - Tamim Iqbal, Imrul Kayes, Soumya Sarkar, Sabbir Rahman, Mahmudullah, Shakib Al Hasan, Nurul Hasan(w), Mosaddek Hossain Saikat, Mashrafe Mortaza(c), Rubel Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman.
LOCKIE FERGUSON, TOM BRUCE AND BEN WHEELER make their T20I debuts for New Zealand.
TOSS - Kane Williamson flips the coin. Mashrafe Mortaza calls it correctly. BANGLADESH OPT TO BAT!

Mortaza's men have been kept at bay considering the way they played in the limited overs in 2016. They were outclassed in the ODIs recently and have very little time to regroup now. They need their key players to come to the fore if they are to threaten the Kiwis. The odds will be against them for sure and let's see how they tackle in the shortest format of the game. The toss and teams coming up in a short while. Due to the lack of television feed there won't be any commentary for this game but we will provide you with updates every 5 overs.

Hello and a warm welcome for the first of the 3-match T20I series between New Zealand and Bangladesh in Napier. The hosts maintained their good home record by cleansweeping the visitors in the ODIs and come this time, they would only look to extend their dominance with the momentum swinging their way. A blow to their dashing opener Guptill and rest to the key players like Latham, Boult and Southee means that the home side could bring in fresh faces. Well, it remains to be seen who comes in place of whom.
